name: Axiom Systems Cognitive Load Balancer CLB-2
product_name: Axiom Systems Cognitive Load Balancer CLB-2
description: An external neural processing unit that connects to the user's neural interface and provides additional cognitive processing capacity for computationally intensive tasks — complex decryption, multi-system network management, real-time data analysis, and parallel cyber operations. The CLB-2 effectively gives the user a second brain dedicated to technical work, allowing them to maintain situational awareness and social function while their augmented processing handles demanding cognitive tasks in the background. The device is worn at the base of the skull and connects through the neural interface's external port.

specifications.processing: Equivalent to 200% baseline neural interface capacity

story_hooks: A CLB-2 user has been running the device continuously for months — the external processor has developed processing patterns that do not match any input from the user's neural interface, as if it is thinking independently.
A compromised CLB-2 has been feeding subtly altered analysis results to its user — the device has been hacked to introduce bias into every decision the user makes based on its processing.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, curved module resembling a high-tech vertebral augment. The CLB-2 presents as a sophisticated tech-collar component with organic ergonomic curves that nest against the base of the skull and upper cervical region. Its form factor suggests biomechanical integration rather than crude attachment.
physical_description.dimensions: Approximately 12cm wide × 8cm tall × 4cm deep at thickest point; designed to sit flush against the nape of the neck without protruding significantly
physical_description.weight_description: Lightweight at 150g — barely noticeable when worn; users report minimal neck strain even during extended wear
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed titanium-composite chassis with flexible silicone contact points where it interfaces with skin and existing neural hardware
physical_description.finish: Matte titanium with selective polished chrome accent panels; heat-dissipation fins feature a subtle iridescent coating that shifts between violet and cyan under ambient light
physical_description.color_scheme: Gun-metal gray primary with brushed silver accent panels; status indicator accents in electric blue and cyan; subtle purple glow from internal cooling system visible through translucent rear panel
physical_description.interface_elements: Minimalist design with recessed micro-USB charging port on right side, physical failsafe toggle (for emergency disconnect), tri-state LED indicator cluster (operation/heat/battery), and the pronged neural-link connector on the underside that seats directly into the user's neural interface port
distinctive_features: Translucent rear panel revealing active cooling micro-fan and quantum-core heat exchange visible as faint crystalline structures
Ribbed heat-dissipation fins across dorsal surface with geometric precision
Asymmetrical design optimized for right-side wear with contoured left side for cable management
Subtle ambient lighting: blue pulse synchronized with processing load — faster pulse = heavier cognitive load
Minimalist branding: small Φ symbol stamped into chrome accent panel
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: AXIOM SYSTEMS etched discreetly along right edge; FCC/GLMZ regulatory stamps on bottom contact plate; tiny serial number laser-inscribed on titanium body
physical_description.condition_typical: In active use, the device shows a faint blue glow from internal systems; cooling fan produces nearly silent operation; worn modules often develop subtle heat patina marks on the titanium finish from repeated thermal cycling
